description:
What If You Lived Inside a Ball of a Million Stars?

Episode 117 of a daily journey through the universe. ✨
We fly into a globular cluster: up to a million stars packed into a ball about 100 light-years across, some of the oldest stars in the galaxy at over 12 billion years, about 150 around the Milky Way, Omega Centauri, and the 1974 Arecibo message sent to M13.

➡️ Next stop: Polaris
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

segments.text: What if your night sky had a million stars, and it was never dark?
Imagine a ball of stars. Hundreds of thousands, even a million of them, packed together.
segments.headline: A ball of stars

segments.text: That's a globular cluster. Most are about one hundred light-years across.
If you lived on a planet inside one, the night sky would blaze with thousands of bright stars. Night would never be truly dark.
segments.headline: A sky that's never dark

segments.text: They're among the oldest things in our galaxy. Many of their stars are more than twelve billion years old.

visual.label: years old
visual.sub: older than the Milky Way's disk

segments.text: About one hundred and fifty of them swarm around the Milky Way, like bees around a hive.
segments.headline: 150 around our galaxy

segments.text: The biggest, Omega Centauri, may be the leftover core of a small galaxy we swallowed. It even hides a black hole.
segments.headline: Omega Centauri

segments.text: In nineteen seventy-four, astronomers beamed a radio message toward the cluster M13. It will arrive in about twenty-five thousand years.
segments.headline: A message to M13

segments.text: With binoculars, you can find M13 yourself, as a fuzzy ball in the constellation Hercules.
segments.headline: Find it yourself

segments.text: Next stop: Polaris. Which part surprised you most? Tell me in the comments, and follow for the next stop.
